To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the reliability of interpretation of cineangiograms as a diagnostic tool is dependent on the level of experience of the individual observer, the consistency with which he interprets cineangiograms, and the consistency of the angiographic items he evaluates.

the reliability of interpretation of cineangiograms is related to the consistency of individual observers in their interpretation of angiograms and to the consistency of their interpretations from one reading to another.

interobserver and intraobserver agreement in coronary cineangiography is not uniform for all items, that there are some angiographic items that are relatively easy to agree upon and others that are more difficult, that some observers are more reliable and consistent in reading cineangiograms than others, and that experience and consistency of reading seem to be related to each other.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reliability and validity of coronary angiography as a diagnostic technique.
the problem of observer variation and its effects upon the reliability of interpretation of cineangiograms.
the reliability of coronary cineangiograms and their interpretation as a diagnostic tool in the study of coronary artery disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

there is a high degree of intra- and interobserver agreement on the interpretation of coronary angiograms, but that the degree of consistency varies with the angiographic items and the individual observers.

the reliability of coronary cineangiography is a function of the experience of the observer, the degree of consistency with which the individual observer reads the films, and the consistency with which the observer reads the films on different occasions.
the more experienced the observer, the less likely he is to change his mind about the angiographic findings.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reliability of coronary angiography is not as good as one might wish, but it can be improved by careful training of the observer and by the use of standard definitions of the angiographic items.

the most reliable items in coronary cineangiography are those that can be seen in the most proximal portions of the coronary vessels and that interobserver disagreement is greatest for the most distal portions.
the more experienced the reader, the more consistently he reads the angiogram and the more likely it is that he will agree with the other observers.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the more consistent the reader is in reading the same cineangiogram on two different occasions, the more likely it is that he will agree with other readers and the more likely that he will have had experience in reading cineangiograms.
there is a lot of room for improvement in the quality of coronary cineangiograms as a diagnostic tool.
the more experienced the observer, the more reliable the interpretation of cineangiograms.
